Decision — coding agents as Bus sessions, over ACP

Status: accepted 2026-10-30.

Context

Coding agents (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex, OpenCode) were driven by a separate hand-made path each, and none was a Bus citizen. A running turn could not be watched, steered, answered or stopped from the Bus. Agents already reached into MixOS through mixos-mcp; the missing half was MixOS reaching out to them.

The Agent Client Protocol (ACP, Apache-2.0) is the open standard for that: JSON-RPC 2.0 over an agent's stdio, spoken by all of those agents directly or through a small adapter.

The decision

  1. ACP is a vocabulary, not a wire format. The Bus keeps its own framing. ACP messages never travel raw in a Bus body; one gateway maps them onto ordinary Bus commands and topics.
  2. One gateway: agentd, a Mix Bus citizen (Bus name agent), one per user session. It is the only process that holds ACP pipes, runs each agent as a child on a two-way pipe, and adds no transport or addressing of its own. It starts as a Mix script, per "Mix before another Rust daemon".
  3. The loop: ACP → Bus ← MCP. agentd speaks ACP to the agent and republishes its updates on agent.session.updated; it gives every session a mixos-mcp server, so the agent acts back on the Bus as mcp-s-<session>-….
  4. The client side of ACP is MixOS's.
    • Files (fs/*) are confined to the session's cwd and additional_dirs, which must lie under the instance's configured roots (paths resolved, no symlink or .. escape).
    • Terminals (terminal/*) run on pipes with a bounded output tail on the headless path; on a desk they are to move onto Term.
    • Permission requests go to a human through notifyd, or to an instance policy that may answer only allow_once. No answer is never yes, and a cancel answers every open request cancelled.
    • This confines what the agent asks agentd for. The agent's own tools (its shell, its built-in file tools) are not confined by agentd, and the decision does not claim a sandbox.
  5. Agent rules still bind. Agents run with the user's real HOME and normal configuration, so their own hooks and instructions apply.
  6. The broker owns the sender. agentd recognises a session's own agent by the Bus name the broker stamps on its requests. A session's own agent cannot act on that session (AGENT_SELF); a session started by an agent is a child, and a child cannot start or resume sessions (AGENT_DEPTH); a hard cap on live sessions (AGENT_LIMIT) holds for everyone.
  7. Every agent.* command answers every caller, per the open Bus. What makes a call safe is the instance: its roots, its permission policy, its caps, and the log. Capability tokens were considered and rejected: they refuse honest callers and leave self-approval one hop away.
  8. Durable intent. agentd writes every acting command and every mapped update to an append-only SQLite log before it runs or publishes it. Command ids are scoped per session; a retry with the same id gets the first reply and never runs again. Sessions outlive agentd in the log, and agent.session.resume brings one back through the agent's own session/resume or session/load.
  9. Versions. ACP v1 is required; v2 is to be negotiated when both sides offer it, behind the same Bus vocabulary.
  10. Foreign code. ACP agents are external programs at the edge, called through Mix process primitives. No ACP SDK enters mix.

Known residuals

  • An agent with a shell can open a Bus client of its own, or register under another name. The sender check catches the honest MCP path only; the cap and the human in the loop catch the rest.
  • The asking agent can reach notifyd through mixos-mcp and answer its own permission question: an accepted consequence of the open Bus.
  • agentd checks a path and then reads or writes it in a separate step; an agent that swaps the path for a symlink in between can lead it out, but doing so takes the agent's own tools, which reach the same files anyway.

Not doing

  • Replacing the Bus wire format with JSON-RPC, or speaking ACP to outside editors directly. An ACP server face for editors could come later, on top of agentd, as its own decision.
  • Merging mixos-mcp into agentd: mixos-mcp serves outside agents too.

Where it stands

agentd, its session log, resume, fs/*, headless terminals and the mix agent command line are in place, tested with Claude (claude-agent-acp), Gemini CLI, OpenCode and Codex (codex-acp). Open: terminals through Term on a desk, ACP v2, and a Workshop front end.
